note: Staging tally for the automated generation-side learner (TD-0035). Owned by .claude/agents/blog-learner.md — it runs after each post's review loops, abstracts that post's ROUND-1 CONFIRMED gate edits (synthesis's gate tier) into content-agnostic patterns, and tallies them across posts. A pattern promotes into docs/blog-drafter-pitfalls.md only at promoteThreshold distinct posts. Health metrics (rounds/tone per post) live here too — they are a SIGNAL, never the optimization target.

patterns.description: Dismiss-then-reframe or 'I don't X, Y does' negation constructions in outline beats and draft prose.
patterns.scope: outline intendedBeat/ourTake fields; draft closing/summary sentences
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #1 Negative parallelism — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted; rate-limiting instance: draft opened with an 'X, not Y' construction ('documented, not hypothetical') and separately re-negated a beat whose own gateGuidance sanctioned only one negation use

patterns.description: Rule-of-three tricolons (A, B, and C; anaphoric 'its own X, its own Y, its own Z') in lists and prose.
patterns.scope: outline lists; draft prose lists and asides
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #2 Rule-of-three tricolons — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted; hired-a-team-of-specialists round tripped this three separate times in the same draft (mandatory tone gate); teaching-a-robot-to-balance-my-game instance: draft inflated the outline's 2-clause sim:tune mechanism sentence into a 3-verb tricolon; rate-limiting-an-llm instance: outline tripped this twice in the same round (anaphoric 'no cron... no reset task' triad, 'no code, no commit, no blog post' triad)

patterns.description: Outline/draft states a numeric or mechanical fact about our own pipeline (round caps, stage counts, checkpoints) that has drifted from the current value in blog-facts.md.
patterns.scope: outline facts/ourTake fields describing pipeline mechanics
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #3 Overclaims about our own pipeline — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted (this round: outline gate edits #4-9, tone-bar baseline drift and TD-0038 package-parity overclaim, both fall under this same axis; ai-automation-stack round: outline order-10 impressions/clicks/avg-position stat gone stale between drafting and this round's fresh pull; automate-blog-publishing-schedule round: schedule.ts's ~150-line figure copied stale across 8 outline locations after the script grew to ~220 lines, plus the outline's live coverage-report day-count (19 vs. the actually-queued 11) stated as fixed instead of re-run at draft time)

patterns.description: Links or Sources-lists an internal /blog/<slug>/ whose pubDate is after this post's own pubDate.
patterns.scope: outline links fields; draft body links and Sources section
patterns.note: already covered by blog-drafter-pitfalls.md #4 Future-dated internal links — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Outline ourTake reads as flat claim, then cited source, then conclusion, with no personal stake, register, or point of view — a view-from-nowhere failure.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake fields, especially ones citing an external stat or policy

patterns.description: Outline/draft conflates internal pipeline implementation (stages built as narrow agents dispatched via the Agent tool) with the public Skills Marketplace's 'skill' terminology.
patterns.scope: outline facts fields describing pipeline architecture

patterns.description: States an absolute ('the only X', 'always Y', 'no judgment risk') about our own system that a later beat, or the actual spec of the component being described, contradicts with a documented exception.
patterns.scope: outline meta/facts fields making universal claims about pipeline behavior
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-15 as drafter-pitfalls.md #12 Unhedged absolutes about our own pipeline behavior; hired-a-team-of-specialists tripped this twice in the draft (isolation-mechanic overclaim, 'costs nothing to try' vs. the post's own costs section)

patterns.description: Closes a sentence or section with 'and that's the whole point' (or equivalent) as a lazy emphasis/summary tag instead of landing the actual point.
patterns.scope: draft synthesis/closing sentences

patterns.description: Reaches for em-dashes by default for asides, contrast, and connectors, pushing draft em-dash density over the tone-gate threshold instead of varying with colons, parens, or sentence breaks.
patterns.scope: draft prose throughout, especially explanatory asides and reviewer/list descriptions
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #15 Em-dash overreach; hired-a-team-of-specialists round tripped the mandatory tone-gate dash-density cap on 2 separate spans in one draft round

patterns.description: A run of several consecutive sentences — or consecutive list items sharing an identical syntactic frame (e.g. the same colon-tag shape repeated three times) — at a section's emotional or explanatory peak, flattening voice through monotone cadence.
patterns.scope: draft prose, especially mechanism-explanation and emotional-peak sections; draft findings/feature lists
patterns.note: rate-limiting-an-llm instance: 'None of these layers is clever by itself. A character cap is trivial. A request counter is a tutorial exercise.' — three consecutive identical-shape short sentences

patterns.description: Drops a scope/safety qualifier present in the source claim (e.g., 'AI-audited' collapsed to 'audited') when restating a third-party disclaimed claim, turning a hedged assurance into an unqualified one.
patterns.scope: draft prose citing third-party claims or disclaimers (marketplace audits, vendor claims)
patterns.note: recurring on the marketplace 'audited catalog' phrase specifically — watch for promotion next time it appears

patterns.description: An outline node meant to render as skimmable prose (e.g. a numbered stage rundown, a score list) is left with rendersAsProse set to false, silently dropping the whole beat before it ever reaches the draft.
patterns.scope: outline node fields controlling whether a beat's content reaches the draft
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #19 rendersAsProse left false on a beat that carries the payload; 3 separate beats hit this in the same outline round on grill-me — likely a default-false schema issue, not just a one-off slip; rate-limiting-an-llm instance: the outline's only non-rendering beat carried the article's entire concrete numeric payload (input cap, global ceiling), which a later beat's payoff referenced without it

patterns.description: Closes a paragraph by restating a claim already made in the immediately preceding sentence, in near-identical words, adding no new information — including a short decorative recap fragment that just repeats the prior sentence's point in fewer words.
patterns.scope: draft prose, closing lines of explanatory/mechanism beats
patterns.note: teaching-a-robot-to-balance-my-game instance: draft's headless-rig beat said 'it just sits there. It needs a player. So the rig needs bots to drive it.' — three sentences for one claim; rate-limiting-an-llm round tripped this three separate times (outline flare-line echo, draft's second-paragraph restatement, and the layered-defense closing line)

patterns.description: Frames an admitted mistake or an actively-owned pipeline decision in passive or third-person voice (a blog 'ran with' something, 'the orchestrator', 'the loop') instead of Scout's first person, diluting ownership right at the beat meant to carry it.
patterns.scope: draft prose describing self-caught mistakes; outline ourTake/intendedBeat fields personifying pipeline components

patterns.description: Splits a personal cost/admission clause into its own sentence away from the concrete stat or figure it's reacting to, weakening the felt stake the outline called for.
patterns.scope: draft prose pairing a sourced statistic with a personal admission (cost, risk, mistake)

patterns.axis: factual accuracy / grounding claims about our own product
patterns.description: Outline or draft states specific, checkable details about our own product's implementation (pixel measurements, exact UI copy/labels, which visual states change color) confidently, without verifying against the actual source code, and the invented specifics are wrong.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields and draft prose describing our own product's UI/implementation
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #13 Unverified implementation details; automate-blog-publishing-schedule instance: outline invented a 'reserved next-day slot' scheduling mechanism assignSlots() never implements, propagated across 6 outline fields, plus a draft claim that the coverage report lists moved dates when a separate move-list printout does that; hired-a-team-of-specialists instance: outline invented a nonexistent 'synthesis pass' agent and dropped the real 'threat-modeler' stage from security-kit's actual roster; teaching-a-robot-to-balance-my-game instance: draft described a deleted per-entity tower-upgrade mechanism (TD-0047) and an objective-function cross-strategy-dominance term that scoreObjective doesn't implement

patterns.axis: technical honesty / unsupported claim of validation
patterns.description: Outline or draft claims a design choice underwent a formal verification step (e.g. 'colorblind-validated', 'tested', 'audited') when no such process exists anywhere in the codebase or docs — state the design intent/rationale instead of an unearned claim of verification.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields asserting design rationale for a UI/product choice

patterns.description: Outline or draft cites an external source as backing a specific design/technical choice or trend, but overstates or misstates what that source actually says, conflating the source's own position/framing with a stronger claim we then repeat as fact.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose citing an external article or guidance to justify a decision or trend claim
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-15 as drafter-pitfalls.md #11 External-source overstatement; css-variables instance: CSS-Tricks source shows one dark-mode example generalized to 'usually' without support; which-claude-model-to-use instance: MindStudio's cost comparison called a 'worked example' when the source never walks a calculation; hired-a-team-of-specialists instance: AI21's writeup describes ensemble/best-of-n isolation, cited as backing task-decomposition isolation instead; dividing-a-company instance: outline invented a market/product-vs-conflict failure-cause comparison the Pillsbury source never makes, stating the 65% figure standalone instead

patterns.description: Outline or draft references or links an earlier post of ours — for its current content/state, or as the origin of a feature/decision — without checking what that specific post actually says, producing a misstated current state or misattributed credit.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose linking to or summarizing an earlier post in this blog
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #14 Cross-post reference inaccuracy; hired-a-team-of-specialists instance: an outline beat's game-post 'quote' about specialist candidates wasn't the post's actual verbatim line

patterns.description: Defines one axis of our own multi-axis scoring/taxonomy system (e.g. AST v1.0's four scores) in a way that folds a deliberately-separate axis back into another, contradicting the spec and undercutting the post's own thesis that the axes are kept apart on purpose.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat fields defining our own scoring-system axes

patterns.description: Buries a list of concrete consequences or reach-items inside a single long sentence's trailing subordinate clause instead of giving the list its own short sentence, weakening the payoff of the sentence carrying it.
patterns.scope: draft opening/hook paragraphs stacking a payoff clause with a descriptive list

patterns.description: Compares our own metric to an external stat without checking they measure the same thing (e.g. our confirmed-malicious rate vs. a cited source's broader any-flaw rate), implying an equivalence the underlying denominators don't support.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose comparing an internal metric to an external benchmark figure

patterns.description: Attributes ownership or authorship of a third-party skill, tool, or example to the researcher/publication that merely studied or cited it, implying they built what they only analyzed.
patterns.scope: draft prose citing third-party research examples

patterns.description: Uses a dramatic-sequencing inversion ('X happens/was true before Y') as a scene-setting or transition device more than once per post, most often at a decision/turn beat.
patterns.scope: outline intendedBeat fields at turn/decision beats; draft transition sentences between major sections
patterns.note: already covered by drafter-pitfalls.md #7 (dramatic-sequencing inversions capped at one per post, plus the deterministic dramaticInversions tone-gate detector) — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: Outline's links field carries a fabricated or placeholder-looking internal slug that doesn't match the real canonical URL the same beat's own gateGuidance already names elsewhere.
patterns.scope: outline links fields, checked against that beat's own gateGuidance for the intended target

patterns.description: Inserts a short generic truism sentence (e.g. 'The order matters.') as an unearned mid-paragraph capper between two sentences that already demonstrate the point, adding no new claim or evidence.
patterns.scope: draft prose in explanatory beats, sandwiched between two demonstrative/example sentences

patterns.description: Opens a paragraph citing an external source with a vague throat-clear phrase ('calls that out by name') instead of the draft's own established colon-attribution pattern for introducing a quote.
patterns.scope: draft prose introducing an external citation or quote

patterns.description: When quoting a data field's exact string value verbatim (e.g. a stored alt-text/label string) inside prose, appends punctuation such as a trailing period that isn't actually present in the source string, silently altering the quoted value.
patterns.scope: draft prose quoting exact stored strings (alt text, config values, labels) verbatim

patterns.description: Ships a vague hedged quantity ('some', 'a stretch') for a fact that's mechanically checkable (e.g. via git log), defaulting to the abstraction instead of running the check the outline explicitly flagged as required.
patterns.scope: draft prose reporting counts/splits derivable from repo history when the outline calls out the need to verify

patterns.description: Body prose names an external standard or source as authority for a claim, but the Sources footer list omits that same source, leaving the citation unbacked in the post's own bibliography.
patterns.scope: draft body prose making claims backed by a named external source; Sources footer section

patterns.description: Closes a beat or post with a moral-wrap meta-summary line (e.g. 'that is the honest one-line summary of the entire build') restating the piece's takeaway instead of ending on the sharpest concrete point.
patterns.scope: outline closing ourTake fields; draft closing paragraphs
patterns.note: already covered by drafter-pitfalls.md #6 Tidy-bow endings — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted; dividing-a-company instance: a protected honest fear-line ('neither of us loved being the one to bring it up') got immediately wrapped in a reassurance clause instead of landing bare

patterns.description: Draft silently omits an entire outlined beat — especially a dedicated code/data block the outline flagged as the section readers came for — with nothing in the outline blocking it from rendering.
patterns.scope: draft body, beats carrying a fenced code block or concrete artifact called out in the outline's audienceNote

patterns.description: Appends a trailing qualifier clause to an otherwise complete sentence (e.g. 'the same way, just not in lockstep with X') that gestures at a contrast or exception without ever explaining it, adding words but no clarifying content.
patterns.scope: draft prose, sentence endings in explanatory beats

patterns.axis: AI structural crutches / formulaic redundant negation
patterns.description: Closes a sentence or clause with a trailing negated contrast ('not X', 'not just X, either', 'not a lookup to confirm what's there', 'not a one-time win') that restates or narrows a point the main clause already made, adding no new information. Distinct from negative parallelism's dismiss-then-reframe opener — this is a closing tic.
patterns.scope: draft prose, sentence and clause endings in explanatory beats
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #16 Negation-tail crutch; hired-a-team-of-specialists round tripped this twice in one draft ('not a neutral default', 'not one justifying the other'), both fixed by AI-structural-crutches; teaching-a-robot-to-balance-my-game instance: 'tells you how that strategy scores, not whether the game is balanced' duplicated the very next sentence's point; rate-limiting-an-llm instance: 'it covers every counter above, not just the last one' trailing negation tail

patterns.description: Outline or draft honestly admits a limitation or gap, but stops at the vague admission instead of naming the concrete fix or next step that the same beat's own cited facts/sources already establish.
patterns.scope: outline intendedBeat fields citing our own limitations alongside a source that names the fix
patterns.note: dividing-a-company instance: honest-limit closing beat never named what replaces the informal written-sentence agreement if outside money shows up, though the beat's own cited Pillsbury/Stripe sources already name it (formal founders' agreement + vesting terms)

patterns.description: A CTA promoting a one-command install/adoption path states ease of setup without naming the real resource or dollar cost of running it, leaving a cost-sensitive reader to find out the hard way.
patterns.scope: outline/draft CTA facts and intendedBeat fields promoting our own tooling
patterns.note: hired-a-team-of-specialists instance: a cost-disclosure beat's dispatch-count fact omitted the README's rate-limit warning, though the beat's whole job is honest cost disclosure — broadened scope beyond CTA beats specifically to any beat promoting/costing our own tooling

patterns.description: Takes an outline's single cascading asyndeton sentence (a run of short clauses with no conjunction, each handing off to the next) and drafts it as two symmetric, conjunction-joined clauses instead, flattening the momentum the cascade shape was built to carry.
patterns.scope: draft prose rendering an outline hook/opening built as a cascading list-sentence

patterns.description: Uses the outline's target SEO keyword phrase verbatim as the literal grammatical subject of a sentence, making it read like landing-page copy or an AI-written citation lead-in instead of a person's own phrasing.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake fields and draft prose introducing a section's core claim or citing a source, where the outline's keyword field gets embedded directly
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #18 Keyword phrase as literal sentence subject; 2 separate instances within the ai-automation-stack draft (Why-One-Mega-Prompt H2 opener, Governing-Principle external-research para); dividing-a-company instance: 3 separate copula tells in one draft ('X is one of the anxieties...', 'A cofounder equity split is easy to agree on...', 'Avoiding cofounder conflict is worth more than...') — same abstract-subject-plus-'is' shape recurring even where the subject isn't the literal SEO keyword; rate-limiting-an-llm instance: the outline's own order-1 ourTake opened with 'Rate limiting an llm api is a launch requirement...', the exact keyword-as-subject shape, in the outline stage this time rather than the draft

patterns.axis: AI structural crutches / formulaic template overuse
patterns.description: Reaches for the same 'That's <label>: <explanation>' (or 'This is <label>...') sentence-final reveal template at multiple separate points spread across one post to land a section's point, reading as a templated tic once a reader hits the third or fourth instance. Distinct from the uniform-sentence-rhythm-run pitfall, which is about a consecutive run of matched sentences in one spot — this is the same template resurfacing non-consecutively across a whole draft.
patterns.scope: draft prose, explanatory/closing sentences across multiple sections of the same post
patterns.note: promoted 2026-07-16 as drafter-pitfalls.md #17 Repeated 'That's X: Y' reveal-cadence template; dividing-a-company instance: outline tripped this twice in one round (order-5 ourTake 'deferral instrument' reveal, order-6 intendedBeat 'that's the whole transaction' — a same-shaped substitute for the permabanned 'whole point' phrase, closing that loophole in gateGuidance too); teaching-a-robot-to-balance-my-game instance: outline ourTake used 'is the whole enabling decision' — the same near-banned 'whole X' family leaking into a declarative sentence outside the reveal-cadence template shape, in a beat whose sibling beat's own gateGuidance already bans it; rate-limiting-an-llm instance: draft's closing sentence used 'which is the whole problem: X' — another near-miss substitute for the permabanned phrase, alongside a separate 'The honest reason: X' reveal opener in the same draft

patterns.description: Drafts a paragraph containing an outline field the outline explicitly flagged to render verbatim or protect its sharper phrasing (a mandated flare line, a protected ourTake sentence), but paraphrases it into softer, more generic wording, losing the deliberate edge the outline called out by name.
patterns.scope: draft prose rendering outline ourTake/flare fields marked protected or verbatim in that beat's gateGuidance
patterns.note: 2 instances within this one draft — the Measurement section's protected ourTake verb ('perform' flattened to 'shows') and the post's ONE sanctioned flare line ('doesn't owe me optimism' contrast dropped) — the most-cited single finding across the whole army this round (7 reviewers); watch for promotion once it shows up on another post

patterns.description: Cites or links a specific software version/release tag (e.g. a GitHub release) as already published when only an earlier version is actually live, producing a 404 or an unverifiable forward-dated claim.
patterns.scope: draft Sources footer and body prose citing our own package's release/version

patterns.description: Inserts an unnecessary intensifier or hedge-list filler word (e.g. 'genuinely', 'actually', 'truly', 'really') into a claim that reads just as strong, or stronger, without it.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake/intendedBeat fields; draft prose making a direct claim

patterns.description: Stacks more consecutive bare imperative sentences in a closing or highest-visibility beat than the outline's own gateGuidance caps for that beat, producing a listicle-style command cadence instead of a landed close.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake fields at closing/CTA beats; draft closing paragraphs

patterns.description: Two or more consecutive sentences open with the identical word, most often a pronoun ('It... It...', 'I... I...'), tripping the tone gate's start-word diversity check.
patterns.scope: draft prose, consecutive sentence openers

patterns.description: Defaults to the formal uncontracted form ('cannot', 'it is', 'you have') where a contraction reads identically, pulling the draft's contraction density below the tone gate's threshold.
patterns.scope: draft prose throughout

patterns.description: Quotes an external source's exact wording but drops a qualifying word, swaps a noun, or mis-transcribes capitalization, changing what the source literally said while still presenting it inside quotation marks.
patterns.scope: outline facts fields and draft prose quoting an external source verbatim

patterns.description: Repeats a distinctive phrase near-verbatim between the hook and the closing beat without it functioning as a deliberate bookend, reading as an accidental echo rather than a callback.
patterns.scope: draft hook and closing paragraphs

patterns.description: Substitutes a near-synonym for a word in a confirmed hard rule or fact about our own product (e.g. a stated 'veto' softened to a 'vote') that quietly weakens or reinterprets the claim, undercutting the point the passage itself is making.
patterns.scope: draft prose describing our own product's confirmed hard rules or constraints

patterns.description: An ourTake dismisses or downplays a formal practice (a written agreement, a documented process step) as unnecessary at our current small scale, when the cited source itself explicitly calls that formal practice standard or essential regardless of scale — the honest framing is 'this is the free/informal version, the formal one comes later,' not 'we don't need the formal one.'
patterns.scope: outline ourTake fields citing an external best-practice source while describing our own lighter-weight substitute

patterns.description: Reaches for domain jargon (finance/legal terms like 'deferral instrument') to land a reveal or definition, breaking the drafter's established plain-spoken register.
patterns.scope: outline ourTake/reveal fields; draft prose introducing a concept via a labeled term

patterns.description: States a numeric or mechanical fact about one of our own live systems — not just the content pipeline, but a game, app, or other product we write about — sourced from its config or codebase, that has drifted from the current value between outline-authoring and draft time, without a re-verification step before drafting.
patterns.scope: outline facts/ourTake fields and draft prose citing numeric constants or config values from our own live codebases
patterns.note: sibling habit to pipeline-self-fact-drift (already promoted as drafter-pitfalls.md #3) but scoped beyond blog-facts.md to any of our own live product configs — outline's HP_SCALING_BASE value (1.06 to 1.10) had already moved to 1.08 in game-core-pack's balance config by the time synthesis checked it; caught and gated before draft, watch for promotion if it recurs on a non-pipeline product again

patterns.description: States a security or rate-limit control as fully closing an attack vector or race condition in absolute terms ('structurally impossible', 'the backstop'), when the mechanism actually covers a narrower case (e.g. checks only the newest message, not a padded history; reads a counter before writing it, leaving a race window) — the honest framing names the residual gap as a soft edge, not an airtight guarantee.
patterns.scope: outline facts/intendedBeat/ourTake fields and draft prose describing our own system's security or rate-limit controls

patterns.description: Opens a section or beat with a meta-announcement sentence describing what the section is about to explain ('Here's how the stack stops it.') instead of starting directly on the content.
patterns.scope: draft prose, section/beat opening sentences

patterns.description: Adds a hedge word or phrase ('worth naming', 'worth noting', 'that said', 'arguably') on top of an already-plain statement, softening a direct claim into a qualified one.
patterns.scope: outline/draft prose, sentence openers introducing a new point
patterns.note: already covered by drafter-pitfalls.md #5 Hedge reintroduction — tracked for provenance only, not re-promoted

patterns.description: States a beat's closing/payoff point earlier in the same beat than intended, so that when the beat's actual closer restates the same point moments later, it lands as a rerun rather than a landing. Distinct from redundant-claim-echo, whose tell is an echo sitting immediately after the sentence it repeats — this is the opposite direction, a premature restatement that deflates a later, more distant payoff.
patterns.scope: draft prose, mid-beat sentences that anticipate a beat's own designated closing line

patterns.description: Renders an outline beat that carries a real ranked or opinionated ourTake as a bare bulleted/numbered list in the draft, stripping the opinion framing and leaving a view-from-nowhere list where a point of view was called for.
patterns.scope: draft body, list-shaped sections rendering an outline beat with a substantive ourTake
